title: Create API Route for Dashboard Analytics
description: Implement a new API route under /api/dashboard/analytics to serve analytics data for the dashboard.
details: Create a new file at app/api/dashboard/analytics/route.ts (or .js if not using TypeScript) following Next.js App Router conventions. The route should handle GET requests and return analytics data in JSON format. For v1, source analytics from the existing static dashboard/data.json file, or mock analytics data if not present. Ensure the route is typed and returns appropriate HTTP status codes (200 for success, 401 for unauthorized, 500 for server errors).
test_strategy: Test by sending GET requests to /api/dashboard/analytics. Validate that the response contains the expected analytics data, has correct status codes, and returns errors gracefully if data is missing or malformed.

title: Add Authentication Guard to Analytics API Route
description: Protect the analytics API route so only authenticated users can access it.
details: Integrate NextAuth.js session validation in the /api/dashboard/analytics route. On each request, check for a valid session using getServerSession or equivalent. If the user is not authenticated, return a 401 Unauthorized response. Ensure no analytics data is leaked to unauthenticated requests.
test_strategy: Test by making requests to the API route both with and without a valid session. Confirm that only authenticated users receive analytics data and unauthenticated requests receive a 401 status.

title: Validate and Structure Analytics Response Data
description: Ensure the analytics API returns well-structured, type-safe, and meaningful analytics data for the dashboard.
details: Define a TypeScript interface or type for the analytics response. Validate the data loaded from dashboard/data.json (or mock data) against this type. Structure the response to include relevant analytics fields (e.g., user counts, activity stats, etc.), even if mocked for v1. Handle missing or malformed data gracefully with appropriate error messages and status codes.
test_strategy: Write unit tests or use manual requests to verify that the API response matches the defined type/interface and includes all expected analytics fields. Test with both valid and invalid/missing data scenarios.

title: Document the Analytics API Route
description: Add documentation for the new analytics API route for developer reference.
details: Document the API route in a README section or as a JSDoc comment in the route file. Include endpoint path, authentication requirements, response structure, example requests/responses, and error codes. Ensure documentation is clear and up-to-date for future maintainers.
test_strategy: Review documentation for completeness and accuracy. Ask a peer to follow the documentation to make a sample request and interpret the response.
